claim: Access Now #KeepItOn (report launched 2026-03-31): at least 313 internet shutdowns in 52 countries in 2025, up from 304 in 2024, the highest number the coalition has recorded; Myanmar had at least 95.

Access Now #KeepItOn 2025: authorities shut down low-Earth-orbit satellite internet 14 times across seven countries in 2025 (Chad, Equatorial Guinea, Iran, Myanmar, Syria, Tanzania, Yemen), against four such shutdowns in 2024.

ENTSO-E (2026-03-20) published its Expert Panel final report on the 2025-04-28 blackout of continental Spain and Portugal: it resulted from a combination of interacting factors (oscillations, gaps in voltage and reactive-power control, differing voltage regulation practices, rapid output reductions and generator disconnections, uneven stabilisation capability) that led to cascading disconnections. [report PDF not opened; news release only]

China's MOFCOM (statement reported by Global Times, 2025-11-07) suspended, from 2025-11-07 to 2026-11-10, MOFCOM/GAC Announcements 55-58 of 2025 and MOFCOM Announcements 61-62 of 2025 (export controls of 2025-10-09 on superhard materials, rare-earth equipment and materials, medium and heavy rare earths, lithium batteries and graphite anodes, and overseas rare-earth items). [state-media report of a MOFCOM statement; the MOFCOM original was not opened; what happened after 2026-11-10 was not verified]

BIS press release (2025-05-13): Commerce rescinded the AI Diffusion Rule (issued 2025-01-15, compliance due 2025-05-15), said a replacement rule would follow, and added licensing requirements for AI-chip exports to Malaysia and Thailand because of diversion.

15 CFR 742.15(b) (eCFR current): publicly available encryption source code classified 5D002 is not subject to the EAR; a notification to BIS is required only for 'non-standard cryptography'. Compiled images are not source code; they fall under the mass-market route in C-W10-046.

GitHub trade-controls policy: Specially Designated Nationals and other blocked parties may be restricted from GitHub.com; GitHub Enterprise Server and Copilot may not be exported to Country Group E:1 destinations or to Crimea and the separatist areas of Donetsk and Luhansk; Iran is served under an OFAC licence.
Docker Hub usage limits: unauthenticated pulls are limited to 100 per 6 hours per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64; authenticated Personal accounts to 200 per 6 hours; Pro, Team and Business are unlimited.

Bitnami (bitnami/containers issue #83267): from 2025-08-28 Bitnami stopped publishing new images and Helm charts to Docker Hub, moved Debian-based images to a legacy repository, kept free hardened images only on a 'latest' tag, and postponed deletion of the public docker.io/bitnami catalog to 2025-09-29; the source stays on GitHub under Apache-2.0.

Android developer verification: from 2026-09-30, protections apply to users who install apps from participating stores in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand on certified Android 7+ devices; verification expands globally to all apps on certified devices in 2027; a 'power user advanced flow' and limited-distribution accounts launched in August 2026.

European Commission (IP/25/1085, 2025-04-23): first non-compliance decisions under the Digital Markets Act fined Apple EUR 500 million for anti-steering restrictions in the App Store and Meta EUR 200 million for 'consent or pay'.

European Commission Data Act pages: the Data Act (Regulation (EU) 2023/2854) applies since 2025-09-12; users of a connected product may access the data they generate, free of charge; the 'data holder' is typically the manufacturer of the connected product or the provider of the related service (fridge + app example: two data holders).

Data Act Art. 50: 'The obligation resulting from Article 3(1) shall apply to connected products and the services related to them placed on the market after 12 September 2026' (access by design). [verbatim OJ text read on a legal-text mirror; EUR-Lex returned a bot challenge]

European Commission: the Right to Repair Directive (EU) 2024/1799 was adopted 2024-06-13 and had to be transposed and applied from 2026-07-31; manufacturers may not use contractual clauses, hardware or software techniques that impede repair of goods listed in its Annex II unless justified by legitimate and objective factors. [whether any OneMind product category is in Annex II was not checked]

European Commission (2026-04-17): its Sovereign Cloud tender (up to EUR 180 million over 6 years) was awarded to four providers; eligibility required SEAL-2 under the Commission's Cloud Sovereignty Framework, which scores eight objectives including supply-chain transparency and technological openness; most awardees reached SEAL-3.

The four Sovereign Cloud awardees were a Post Telecom-led partnership with OVHcloud and Clever Cloud, STACKIT (Schwarz Group), Scaleway (Iliad) and a Proximus-led partnership using S3NS (a Thales-Google Cloud joint venture), Clarence and Mistral.

Sovereign Tech Fund (Sovereign Tech Agency): invests globally in open digital base technologies; the cost of the proposed work must exceed EUR 50,000; projects already funded by another public entity for the same activities are not eligible.

openDesk grew out of the German Interior Ministry's 'Sovereign Workplace' initiative; ZenDiS GmbH, a publicly funded company of the German federal government, took over its development in January 2024.

Holland & Knight (2025-12-23): the FCC added all foreign-produced unmanned aircraft systems and UAS critical components to the Covered List on 2025-12-22, so they receive no new FCC equipment authorizations; an FCC order of 2025-10-28 set a process that may stop continued import or sale of previously authorized covered equipment. [law-firm summary; FCC public notice not opened (fcc.gov returned 403)]

US Executive Order 'Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence' (2025-12-11): the Attorney General sets up an AI Litigation Task Force within 30 days to challenge state AI laws inconsistent with federal policy, and advisers prepare legislation for a uniform federal AI framework that preempts conflicting state laws.
Debian 'trixie' release page: riscv64 was among the architectures supported at the initial release of Debian 13.0 (2025-08-09); Debian 13.7 was released on 2026-09-12.

Canonical blog: Canonical moved to requiring the RVA23 profile from Ubuntu 25.10, announced it before silicon was available, and supports SpacemiT's K3; Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (RVA20) stays available for earlier RISC-V hardware.

Tom's Hardware, citing SIA data (via TechNews.tw/ITRI): in 2022 Taiwan produced 69% of the world's sub-10nm-class logic and South Korea 31%; SIA projects Taiwan 47% and the US 28% in 2032. [second-hand report of SIA figures]

TrendForce (via I-Connect007): in 2023 Taiwan held about 68% of global capacity at 16/14nm and below, nearly 80% of EUV-generation (7nm and below) capacity, and about 46% of all foundry capacity; it projected the US share of advanced capacity at 17% by 2027.
